The IPCC assessment finds that the potential for direct air carbon capture and storage (5–40 GtCO2 yr–1) is limited mainly by requirements for low-carbon energy and by cost (USD100–300, full range USD84–386, per tCO2) [2].

Across the IPCC chapter's IAM scenarios that limit warming to 2°C (>67%) or lower (categories C1 to C3), the annual DACCS deployment reaches 0 [0–0.02] GtCO2 yr–1 by 2030, 0.02 [0–1.74] GtCO2 yr–1 by 2050, and 1.02 [0–12.6] GtCO2 yr–1 by 2100, where the values are medians and the bracketed values give the 5–95th percentile range [2].
